subject: Media Literacy
title: Television News
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Television News.

hook.text: A TV news segment averages 90 seconds. In that time, you get the story's emotion, not its complexity.

buildup.text: Television news prioritizes visual stories. If there's no footage, the story often gets skipped.

discovery.text: This visual bias means house fires get covered but policy changes that affect millions don't.

twist.text: 24-hour news channels fill time with opinion shows disguised as news, blurring the line completely.

climax.text: Television news shapes what you think about by deciding what's worth showing you.

punchline.text: TV shows what looks dramatic, not what matters most.

quiz.question: What is the 'visual bias' of television news?
options: It prioritizes stories with footage over important but unvisual stories
